primary_source.citation: Yi Yu, Tengyao Wang and Richard J. Samworth, A useful variant of the Davis--Kahan theorem for statisticians, Biometrika 102(2), 2015, 315--323; preprint arXiv:1405.0680.
primary_source.private_comparison_source: A local transcription of the 2014 preprint (SHA-256 ed45f19e...) was used to build prose/distilled_literature/YuWangSamworth2015_statistical_davis_kahan.tex. It is deliberately not distributed, so no row may be resolved by consulting it here.
primary_source.numbering_convention: This census keys on the FLAT preprint numbering used by FinishYuWangSamworth and by the Lean declaration names: Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 3, Theorem 4, Lemma 5. See gap `numbering-conflict` -- the repository's other artifact numbers the same results differently, and the conflict is unresolved.

how_to_use: Two independent axes. `status` is the mathematical judgement against the printed source; `verification` is what the Lean build certifies and is measured, not asserted -- run with `--probe` to resolve every declaration against the real build targets. To find the frontier, filter on `verification`: `absent` rows need new work, `proved_outside_build` rows are already proved and only need wiring into a default target, and `gap_refs` names the specific obstruction in `gaps`. `lean_declarations` names declarations that exist; `planned_declarations` names ones this census wants and nobody has written. Every result in the paper has a row whether or not anything formalizes it -- that is the point of keying on the source rather than on the Lean tree.

status_definitions.compiled_exact: A source-facing theorem matching the printed statement is compiled.
status_definitions.compiled_generalized: The result is compiled in a form strictly stronger or more general than printed (for example any unitarily invariant norm in place of Frobenius, or an intrinsic subspace in place of a matrix of columns).
status_definitions.compiled_specialization: A useful compiled specialization exists, but not the full printed scope.
status_definitions.compiled_corrected: The printed statement is false as transcribed; a corrected statement is compiled, together with a machine-checked refutation of the printed one.
status_definitions.not_represented: No matching declaration was found anywhere in the repository.
status_definitions.not_proof_debt: Exposition, literature comparison, or a definition absorbed into a different formulation. Should be documented but is not formalization debt and must not be counted as a gap.

verification_definitions.proved_in_build: Every declaration resolves against `DavisKahan.All`, which is a default build target. The default build carries no sorry, so this is a proof continuously re-checked by CI.
verification_definitions.proved_outside_build: Every declaration resolves, but only against `FinishYuWangSamworth`, which is NOT a default target. The mathematics is done and compiles; it is not guarded against regression, and a refactor elsewhere can break it while CI stays green.
verification_definitions.partially_in_build: Some declarations resolve against the default build and some only against the completion lane, so the row's source claim is only partly guarded by CI.
verification_definitions.not_applicable: An exposition or literature-comparison item. No formalization is intended, so the row is not proof debt and must not be counted as a gap.

numbering-conflict.title: The repository carries two incompatible numberings for this paper
numbering-conflict.detail: `FinishYuWangSamworth` and every Lean declaration name use a flat sequence -- Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 3, Theorem 4, Lemma 5 -- and cite arXiv:1405.0680. `prose/distilled_literature/YuWangSamworth2015_statistical_davis_kahan.tex` restarts the counter per environment type: its `\sourceanchor` lines name the same rank-one corollary as **Corollary 1**, the same rectangular theorem as **Theorem 3**, and the same appendix lemma as **Appendix Lemma 1**. The two agree only on Theorem 1 and Theorem 2. Neither artifact can settle it, because the transcription both were derived from is not in the tree and the published article is not either. This census keys on the flat sequence because the Lean names do, so that a reader can get from a row to a declaration without a translation table -- that is a tie-break, not a finding. **Resolving it requires one look at the published Biometrika article, and until someone does that, any statement of the form 'we have Theorem 3' is ambiguous in this repository.**

unguarded-completion-lane.title: FinishYuWangSamworth is not a default build target
unguarded-completion-lane.detail: `lakefile.toml`'s `defaultTargets` are `ForMathlib`, `ForTauCeti`, `DavisKahan.All`, `Acharyya2024`, `Acharyya2025`, `DkpsQuench2026` and `Helm2025`. `FinishYuWangSamworth` is a `lean_lib` but not among them, so `lake build` does not compile it and CI does not guard it. Everything the completion lane proves -- Theorem 1's three norm forms, the whole of Theorem 4, Lemma 5, the rank-one singular-vector corollaries, and the corrected equation (4) -- is therefore proved but unprotected. This is the single largest lever on this paper's census: adding one target converts a majority of the `proved_outside_build` rows to `proved_in_build` without any new mathematics. The reason it is not simply done here is that it is a build-policy change affecting every agent's build time, and the lane's own README calls it a deliberately isolated non-default library.

sharpness-examples.title: Neither sharpness example is formalized
sharpness-examples.detail: The paper gives two explicit constructions showing its constants cannot be improved: a diagonal pair whose top-`d` eigenspaces are orthogonal, and a planar rotation model for nearby one-dimensional eigenspaces. Neither is formalized for this paper, and `FinishYuWangSamworth/PROOF_OBLIGATIONS.md` lists both as outstanding. They are mechanical rather than hard: `DavisKahan/FiniteDimensional/Sharpness.lean` already fixes an explicit planar model and computes its singular values by extensional matrix calculation, and `ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/TwoDimensionalSingularValues.lean` exists precisely to serve planar sharpness models. Without them the census can say the bounds hold and cannot say they are sharp -- which is half of what the paper claims.

residual-numerator.title: The sharper residual form of Theorem 2 has no source-facing wrapper
residual-numerator.detail: The proof of Theorem 2 establishes bounds with `‖V-hat Lambda - Sigma V-hat‖_F` in the numerator, and the printed theorem then weakens that to a perturbation norm. The residual machinery is fully proved -- `TauCeti.sq_gap_mul_sum_cross_le_sum_sq_norm_residualColumn` and `TauCeti.sum_sq_norm_residualColumn_le` are exactly it -- but no theorem states the sharper conclusion in the paper's own shape, so a reader cannot cite it. Listed as outstanding by the lane itself.

literal-index-wrappers.title: No wrappers taking literal contiguous indices r..s
literal-index-wrappers.detail: Every formalized statement takes an intrinsic `CorrespondingEigenblock` predicate rather than the paper's literal contiguous index range `r <= j <= s` over a sorted spectrum. That is the better formulation and is why the results generalize past matrices, but it means a statistician holding the paper cannot match hypotheses by inspection. The lane lists optional literal-index wrappers as remaining source-fidelity work.

not-proof-debt.title: Exposition and literature comparison
not-proof-debt.detail: Section 3's audit of statistical applications makes claims about other authors' proof patterns, not new perturbation theorems. It should be documented and must not be counted as a formalization gap.

private-helper-only.title: Some source content exists only as a `private` helper
private-helper-only.detail: Three declarations this census initially cited turned out to be `private`: `sinThetaFrobenius_eq_sqrt_sum_cross` (ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/YuWangSamworth/Statistics.lean), `yuWangSamworth_gram_alignedBasis_le` and `rectangularFrobenius_comp_adjoint_linearIsometry` (FinishYuWangSamworth). They compile and are correct, and they cannot be cited from outside their module. **A `#check` cannot tell a private declaration from a deleted one** -- both fail identically -- which is why the probe now reports the two cases separately; conflating them would let a census report proved mathematics as absent, or absent mathematics as proved. For two of the three the row has a public sibling and nothing is lost. `YWS-S1-complement-identity` had no public sibling -- the identity `‖V_1^T V-hat‖_F = ‖sin Theta‖_F` was proved and unciteable -- and was **fixed on 2026-07-29** by making that one declaration public. The remaining two are genuine internal factoring steps and should stay private.

items.title: Principal angles, sin-Theta, and the Frobenius sine identity
items.summary: For V, V-hat with orthonormal columns the principal angles are the arccosines of the singular values of V-hat^T V, and the Frobenius sine distance satisfies ‖sin Theta‖_F^2 = d - ‖V-hat^T V‖_F^2.
items.notes: The Lean development defines the sine distance intrinsically on subspaces rather than on a matrix of chosen columns, and then proves it agrees with the span-based form. That is why no basis is a hypothesis anywhere downstream. The bridge lemma `sinThetaFrobenius_eq_sqrt_sum_cross` was `private` until 2026-07-29 and is now public.

items.title: ‖V_1^T V-hat‖_F = ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F
items.summary: The cross-block energy against an orthonormal complement of V equals the Frobenius sine distance.
items.notes: Closed 2026-07-29. The identity was proved all along but the declaration was `private`, so nothing outside its module could cite it and this row correctly read `absent` -- the one item in this census where the mathematics existed and the API did not. It is now public, with a docstring saying why. **The census is what found it**: a coverage claim assembled from the Lean side would have counted the proof and never noticed that no reader could reach it.

items.title: Procrustes alignment: ‖V-hat O - V‖_F <= sqrt 2 ‖sin Theta‖_F
items.summary: Minimizing over orthogonal O gives ‖V-hat O - V‖_F^2 = 2 sum (1 - cos theta_j) <= 2 sum sin^2 theta_j.
items.notes: The sqrt-2 step is the whole reason the aligned-basis constant is 2^{3/2} rather than 2. It lives in ForTauCeti as a reusable orthonormal-family result, not as a matrix Procrustes computation.

items.title: Theorem 1 -- the statistical Davis--Kahan baseline (mixed gap)
items.summary: With a mixed spectral separation delta > 0 between the perturbed and population blocks, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= ‖Sigma-hat - Sigma‖_F / delta; the paper notes both norms may be replaced by the operator norm or any orthogonally invariant norm.
items.notes: The paper's 'any orthogonally invariant norm' remark is the primary Lean statement, not an afterthought: `yuWangSamworth_theorem1_uiNorm_le` takes a `UnitarilyInvariantNorm` and the Frobenius and operator forms are its specializations. So the strongest advertised form is the one that is proved.
items.next_action: Wire FinishYuWangSamworth into a default target, or migrate these three into DavisKahan/Specialized.

items.title: Equation (1) -- the eigenvector specialization of the baseline
items.summary: For r = s = j the baseline specializes to a single-eigenvector sine bound with a mixed gap, and after choosing the sign so v-hat^T v >= 0, ‖v-hat - v‖ <= sqrt 2 sin theta.
items.notes: The sign-choice half is available as the rank-one case of the aligned-basis machinery rather than as a separate mixed-gap statement; the census does not claim a source-shaped wrapper for equation (1) itself.
items.next_action: Optional: state equation (1) with literal index j and a mixed gap, purely for source recognizability.

items.title: Theorem 2, first conclusion -- the population-gap sine bound
items.summary: With only the two exterior POPULATION gaps Delta = min(lambda_{r-1} - lambda_r, lambda_s - lambda_{s+1}) > 0, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= 2 min(sqrt d ‖E‖_op, ‖E‖_F) / Delta.
items.notes: This is the paper's headline and it is the best-guarded result in the census: it is in the default build AND pinned by comparator/pending-yu-wang-samworth.json, whose Leaderboard runs `#print axioms TauCeti.sqrt_sum_cross_le_of_population_gap`. The min over the dimension-scaled operator norm and the Frobenius norm is proved as printed, not as one branch.

items.title: Theorem 2, second conclusion -- existence of an aligned orthogonal frame
items.summary: There exists O-hat in O(d) with ‖V-hat O-hat - V‖_F <= 2^{3/2} min(sqrt d ‖E‖_op, ‖E‖_F) / Delta.
items.notes: Stated as the existence of two orthonormal families spanning U and V with the bound on the sum of squared differences, which is the basis-free content of 'there exists an orthogonal alignment'. Constant 2 * sqrt 2 = 2^{3/2} as printed.

items.title: Theorem 2's sharper residual forms
items.summary: The proof actually establishes ‖sin Theta‖_F <= ‖V-hat Lambda - Sigma V-hat‖_F / Delta and the aligned form with sqrt 2 times the same residual; the printed theorem weakens the residual to a perturbation norm.
items.notes: The mathematics is entirely present and in the default build -- the residual columns and the gap-times-cross-energy sandwich are exactly this. What is missing is a theorem whose CONCLUSION is the sharper printed inequality, so the row is generalized-but-unwrapped rather than complete.
items.next_action: Add two wrappers concluding the residual-numerator inequalities directly.

items.title: The residual is bounded by 2 sqrt d ‖E‖_op
items.summary: The step that turns the residual numerator into the dimension-scaled operator-norm branch of the min.
items.notes: This is the half of the proof that produces the sqrt d, and therefore the half that explains why the paper's numerator is a minimum rather than a single norm.

items.source_anchor: Section 2, sharpness example with orthogonal target subspaces
items.title: Sharpness example: orthogonal top-d eigenspaces
items.summary: Sigma = diag(3,...,3,1,...,1) and Sigma-hat = diag(2-eps,...,2-eps,2,...,2) have orthogonal top-d eigenspaces, forcing ‖V-hat O - V‖_F = sqrt(2d) for every O and matching the aligned-basis constant up to (1+eps).
items.notes: Nothing in the repository formalizes this. Its absence is why the census can certify the paper's upper bounds but cannot certify that its constants and dimension dependence are unimprovable -- and the second claim is a substantial part of what makes the paper 'useful'.
items.next_action: Formalize the diagonal pair and the orthogonality of the top-d eigenspaces; the bound then follows from the aligned-basis identity already proved.

items.source_anchor: Section 2, sharpness scale for nearby one-dimensional eigenspaces
items.title: Sharpness example: planar rotation, nearby one-dimensional eigenspaces
items.summary: Sigma = diag(3,1) and Sigma-hat = R_eps Sigma R_eps^T give sin Theta = eps against a bound of 2 eps, so the sine bound is tight up to 2 and the vector bound up to 2^{3/2} even at small angles.
items.notes: Mechanical rather than hard. `DavisKahan/FiniteDimensional/Sharpness.lean` already fixes a single explicit planar model for the Davis--Kahan sharpness results and computes its singular values extensionally, and `ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/TwoDimensionalSingularValues.lean` exists to serve exactly this kind of model.
items.next_action: Instantiate the existing planar sharpness model at Sigma = diag(3,1) and the rotation R_eps.

items.title: Equation (4) -- the double-angle identity, FALSE AS PRINTED
items.summary: The paper rewrites sin^2(2 theta) in terms of ‖v-hat - v‖^2. The printed right-hand side omits a square on the factor (2 - ‖v-hat - v‖^2).
items.notes: This is the census's one genuine source defect and it is machine-checked in both directions: the corrected identity is proved, and the printed polynomial is refuted by `norm_num` at inner product 3/5. Substituting t = ‖v-hat - v‖^2 = 2 - 2c gives sin^2(2 theta) = (1/4) t (2-t)^2 (4-t), and the printed form has (2-t) to the first power. The distilled tex reproduced the ERRONEOUS printed form at its equation (YWS-3) until 2026-07-29, so the repository asserted the false identity in one artifact while refuting it in another; the tex is now corrected, carries the derivation, and cross-references both Lean theorems.
items.next_action: None. Both artifacts now agree and both directions are machine checked.

items.title: Corollary 3 -- the rank-one (single eigenvector) form
items.summary: With Delta_j = min(lambda_{j-1} - lambda_j, lambda_j - lambda_{j+1}) > 0, sin Theta(v-hat, v) <= 2 ‖E‖_op / Delta_j, and after sign alignment ‖v-hat - v‖ <= 2^{3/2} ‖E‖_op / Delta_j.
items.notes: The Lean statement produces a unit scalar c with ‖c • v - u‖ <= 2 sqrt 2 ‖B - A‖ / Delta, which is the sign choice in the RCLike setting -- over the reals c = +-1 recovers the printed statement, and over the complexes a phase is the honest generalization. The distilled tex calls this Corollary 1; see gap `numbering-conflict`.

items.title: Section 3 -- audit of how statisticians actually apply Davis--Kahan
items.summary: A diagnosis of existing proof patterns: authors apply a mixed-gap theorem then invoke Weyl to recover a population gap; spectral-clustering variants hide an interval-counting requirement; Theorem 2 removes both steps.
items.notes: Literature comparison, not a theorem. It is recorded because a census that silently omits a section cannot be read as a coverage claim -- the reader cannot tell an omission from an absence.
items.next_action: None. Do not count this row as a gap.

items.title: Theorem 4 -- right singular subspaces, population squared-singular gap
items.summary: For rectangular A, A-hat with D = A-hat - A and Delta_sv = min(sigma_{r-1}^2 - sigma_r^2, sigma_s^2 - sigma_{s+1}^2) > 0, ‖sin Theta(V-hat, V)‖_F <= 2 (2 sigma_1 + ‖D‖_op) min(sqrt d ‖D‖_op, ‖D‖_F) / Delta_sv.
items.notes: Split across two homes, which is why this row is only partly guarded: the subspace definition and a sine bound are in the default build via ForTauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/YuWangSamworth/SingularSubspace.lean, but the exact paper coefficient (2 sigma_1 + ‖D‖_op) lives in the completion lane. The route is the paper's own: transport to squared Gram operators, then apply the symmetric theorem.
items.next_action: Guard the completion lane, or migrate the coefficient theorems into DavisKahan/Specialized.

items.title: Theorem 4 -- the identical statement for left singular subspaces
items.summary: The paper states that the identical bounds hold for the corresponding left singular-vector blocks U, U-hat.
items.notes: Proved as its own statement rather than by an adjoint-symmetry argument from the right-hand case, so the two are independently checkable.

items.title: Theorem 4 -- the aligned-frame conclusion, both sides
items.summary: Some O-hat in O(d) satisfies ‖V-hat O-hat - V‖_F <= 2^{3/2} (2 sigma_1 + ‖D‖_op) min(sqrt d ‖D‖_op, ‖D‖_F) / Delta_sv, and likewise on the left.
items.notes: Factored through a single generic Gram transport result so that no perturbation argument is duplicated between the symmetric and rectangular cases. That transport result (`yuWangSamworth_gram_alignedBasis_le`) is `private`, which is the right call for an internal factoring step and is why it is not listed here.

items.title: Rank-one singular-vector corollaries (beyond the printed paper)
items.summary: Direct right and left single-singular-vector bounds, obtained by reusing the symmetric rank-one theorem on Gram operators.
items.notes: The paper does not print these; the lane adds them because the rectangular rank-one case is what applications actually use. Recorded so that the census is not read as claiming they are source items.

items.title: Appendix equations (10)-(12) -- the Gram transport identities
items.summary: The identities converting a rectangular perturbation bound into a symmetric one on A^T A and A A^T, producing the (2 sigma_1 + ‖D‖_op) coefficient.
items.notes: Proved for both the Frobenius and operator branches separately, which is what makes the min in Theorem 4's numerator legitimate rather than a bound on one branch quoted for both.

items.title: The self-adjoint dilation route is a modern alternative, not the paper's
items.summary: The repository additionally proves the singular-subspace bound through the Hermitian dilation [[0, A*],[A, 0]] rather than through squared Gram matrices.
items.notes: Mathematically equivalent to the paper's route and recorded here explicitly so that nobody attributes it to Yu, Wang and Samworth. The distilled tex's transcription audit makes the same point.
items.next_action: None. Keep the attribution note attached to these declarations.

items.title: Lemma 5, inequality half -- orthogonal compression cannot increase the Frobenius norm
items.summary: If U and W have orthonormal columns then ‖U^T M W‖_F <= ‖M‖_F.
items.notes: Restated as a two-sided ideal estimate for the rectangular Frobenius norm rather than copied as a matrix-only helper, with bundled linear-isometry wrappers exposing the paper's orthonormal-column hypothesis directly. The distilled tex calls this Appendix Lemma 1; see gap `numbering-conflict`.

items.title: Lemma 5, equality half -- orthonormal rows give equality
items.summary: If instead U and W have orthonormal rows then ‖U^T M W‖_F = ‖M‖_F.
items.notes: The equality half is the direction the appendix proof actually consumes; the inequality half is the one usually quoted. Both are proved. The row-side norm-preservation step `rectangularFrobenius_comp_adjoint_linearIsometry` is `private`; both public forms are listed.
